title: Sorry, I Can't Help You Right Now
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article argues that a genuinely collaborative team culture doesn't emerge organically — it requires explicit, repeated expectation-setting by the leader. In highly collaborative workplaces, the most senior and influential team members are just as willing to help a junior colleague as they are their own leader, and they proactively look for who needs support rather than waiting to be asked. The piece describes how leaders build this culture: modeling the behavior themselves, privately confronting violations, and consistently reinforcing the expectation in group settings until it becomes the team norm. It closes by citing research linking high team collaboration to greater engagement, productivity, and adaptability.
points: Genuine team-wide collaboration is rare and doesn't develop organically — it requires explicit, repeated expectation-setting from the leader.
In highly collaborative teams, status and seniority don't affect who offers support; senior members help junior ones without being asked.
Building this culture requires leaders to model the behavior, confront violations privately, and reinforce the expectation repeatedly in group settings.
Research links high-collaboration teams to greater engagement, productivity, innovation, and adaptability.
quotes: Presuming a team or organization will naturally develop a highly collaborative spirit of working together doesn’t make it so.
the most senior, tenured, experienced, and influential team members are just as willing to lend a hand to a junior colleague as they are to their leader.
Developing such a collective team spirit almost always starts with an explicit expectation by the leader.
Research confirms that teams high in collaboration are more engaged, more productive, more innovative, and more adaptive to change.
When those too busy or important to support others learn from you that their behavior is unacceptable, they quickly get in line and conform to the group norm.
